nd-agr-2026-thompson-vern.name: Vern Thompson
nd-agr-2026-thompson-vern.bio: Former member of the North Dakota House and Senate.

positions.stance: Will refuse to meet in secret executive sessions of the Industrial Commission; "No more sweetheart deals for billionaires."
Will hold regular in-person town halls to share what is going on in Bismarck and listen to communities.
Will testify in legislative committees on behalf of residents' interests, "not the interests of multi-billion dollar out-of-state corporations."
Will fight for fair commodity and input prices and add ag credit counselors to the North Dakota Mediation Service.
Will champion a meatpacking co-op to bring fair prices for producers and quality local meat to consumers.

nd-tax-2026-kroshus-brian.name: Brian Kroshus
nd-tax-2026-kroshus-brian.bio: North Dakota Tax Commissioner since 2022; former North Dakota Public Service Commissioner and private-sector business leader.

positions.stance: "Fairness, transparency and protecting taxpayer dollars are my top priorities."
Believes in "limited government, conservative values, respecting citizen's rights" and applying those ideals to how government works.
Will foster public-private partnerships and support business development to drive long-term economic growth and new job opportunities.

nd-psc-2026-haugen-hoffart-sheri.name: Sheri Haugen-Hoffart
nd-psc-2026-haugen-hoffart-sheri.bio: North Dakota Public Service Commissioner since 2022; former Deputy State Treasurer and electric cooperative board chair.

positions.stance: Stands for "protecting taxpayers by keeping government accountable."
Stands for "defending reliable energy that powers North Dakota homes, farms, and businesses."
Stands for "supporting rural communities with fair and dependable service."
Stands for "securing our future with strong cybersecurity and infrastructure safeguards."

nd-psc2-2026-kringstad-jill.name: Jill Kringstad
nd-psc2-2026-kringstad-jill.bio: North Dakota Public Service Commissioner, appointed in January 2025.

positions.stance: Will fight for "affordable, reliable, dispatchable energy that supports families, farms, and businesses."
Will fight for consumer protection "through accurate utility billing, fair rates, and oversight of critical infrastructure."
Will fight for "fair markets and transparent regulation that send the right signals to utilities and developers."
Will seek stronger regional leadership so North Dakota has influence in grid and infrastructure decisions.
Will fight for "accountability and oversight that protects consumers and fosters innovation."

nd-psc2-2026-kelsh-scot.name: Scot Kelsh
nd-psc2-2026-kelsh-scot.bio: Former North Dakota state representative (1996-2014) and firefighter; tutor and special education behavior technician with Fargo Public Schools.

positions.stance: Supports "responsible data center development that doesn't drive up utility costs for everyday ratepayers."
Committed to "protecting landowners from eminent domain overreach."
Wants to ensure "new industrial development actually benefits the communities it moves into."

dc-mayor-2026-lewis-george-janeese.name: Janeese Lewis George
dc-mayor-2026-lewis-george-janeese.bio: Ward 4 Councilmember and former prosecutor at the DC Office of the Attorney General.

positions.stance: Will strengthen and expand rent stabilization, reform zoning and permitting to build more housing, and launch publicly owned mixed-income housing.
Will expand vocational programs and registered apprenticeships, enforce wage theft laws, and establish a Federal Workforce Transition Center for displaced federal workers.
Supports universal affordable childcare in which families spend no more than 7% of household income on childcare.
Will implement a public safety strategy addressing prevention, intervention, and enforcement, including Community Hubs in all eight Wards.
Will unify the truancy system under one agency, expand after-school programming in all eight Wards, and expand the school workforce.

dc-chair-2026-mendelson-phil.name: Phil Mendelson
dc-chair-2026-mendelson-phil.bio: Chairman of the Council of the District of Columbia since 2012; first elected to the Council as an At-Large Councilmember in 1998.

positions.stance: Promises to "fight to keep DC's local democracy every day" against efforts to overturn DC home rule.
Believes government "should be an honest, efficient deliverer of services" and can accomplish this "without increasing the tax burdens" on residents.

dc-chair-2026-prudent-abi-ananiah.name: Abi-Ananiah Prudent
dc-chair-2026-prudent-abi-ananiah.bio: Community advocate with experience in nonprofit leadership, recruitment, and community engagement.

positions.stance: Will strengthen safety-net services, include local small businesses in city initiatives, and work to improve literacy and math outcomes.
Supports stronger agency oversight, "transparent budgeting, clear performance standards, and consistent tracking of agency outcomes."
Will prioritize funding for proven violent crime reduction strategies focused on repeat violent offenders and expand youth prevention programs.
Supports funding reliable transit, safer streets and intersections, and maintaining roads, bridges, and public infrastructure.

dc-ag-2026-rivera-manuel.name: Manuel Rivera
dc-ag-2026-rivera-manuel.bio: Washington, D.C. attorney and founding attorney of The Law Offices of Manuel Rivera, Esq. & Associates.

positions.stance: Will focus prosecution resources on repeat violent offenders and serious juvenile crime, and prioritize gun offenses and organized retail theft.
Will enforce housing and consumer protection laws, targeting fraud, illegal rental practices, and landlords who violate tenant protection statutes.
Will enforce wage, labor, and consumer laws fairly and establish a Small Business Legal Fairness initiative.
Will publish performance metrics for the office, including case resolution timelines, consumer recoveries, and enforcement outcomes.
Will "aggressively enforce consumer protection and data privacy laws" and seek meaningful restitution for victims.

dc-ag-2026-schwalb-brian.name: Brian L. Schwalb
dc-ag-2026-schwalb-brian.bio: Attorney General of the District of Columbia.

positions.stance: Priorities under "Safer" include prosecuting juvenile crime, holding opioid profiteers accountable, and suing slumlords for dangerous housing conditions.
Priorities under "Stronger" include stopping the federal government's attempted takeover of MPD and opposing unlawful federal orders in court.
Priorities under "Affordable" include getting workers owed wages, securing rent refunds for tenants, and protecting seniors from scams.

dc-shadowsen-2026-strauss-paul.name: Paul Strauss
dc-shadowsen-2026-strauss-paul.bio: District of Columbia shadow U.S. Senator; attorney and former local elected official.

positions.stance: Campaign "fights for DC's Statehood" and works to make sure D.C. has a real voice in Congress.
"DC needs full political equality, self-determination and DC Statehood."
Says school property taxes are tied to state pension underfunding and has "a plan to fix this" that will lower taxes.
Priority: "Transparent public finances — open books, clear reporting, no surprises."
Priority: "Lowering the tax burden so people can stay in their homes."
Priority: "Resilient local communities built on responsible, long-term stewardship."
Priority: "Educating the younger population so they can establish a future in Vermont."

vt-treas-2026-pieciak-mike.name: Mike Pieciak
vt-treas-2026-pieciak-mike.bio: Vermont State Treasurer; former Commissioner of the Vermont Department of Financial Regulation.

positions.stance: Cites a $2 billion cut to unfunded pension liabilities through a compromise with lawmakers and unions protecting teacher and state employee retirement.
Launched Vermont Saves for workers whose employers offer no retirement plan, at no cost to employers.
Supports First Steps Forward, providing $3,200 for every child born on Medicaid to grow until adulthood.
Invests in Vermont's communities "to create a better future for generations to come."
Committed up to $130 million in low-interest loans to build workforce housing through the "10% in Vermont" program.

vt-sos-2026-copeland-hanzas-sarah.name: Sarah Copeland Hanzas
vt-sos-2026-copeland-hanzas-sarah.bio: Vermont Secretary of State since 2022; served 18 years in the Vermont House of Representatives.

positions.stance: Values transparency in elections, including Open Meeting Law trainings, a universal voting guide, and an updated Vermont Election Management System.
Advocates modernizing the Safe at Home program to protect people vulnerable to domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking.
Promotes civics education in schools, voter registration drives, support for local media, and engagement with business leaders.

vt-aud-2026-ashe-tim.name: Tim Ashe
vt-aud-2026-ashe-tim.bio: Former Deputy State Auditor, State Senator, municipal official, affordable housing developer, and congressional aide.

positions.stance: Says preventing fraud, waste, and abuse through comprehensive systems "must always be central to the office's work."
Will identify ways to lower health costs, analyze wait times, and review state health care spending including prescriptions.
Will assess state housing programs for cost, affordability, and geographic equity and quantify effects of short-term rentals and speculative ownership.
Will review Vermont's exposure to changes in federal funding and identify areas of greatest vulnerability.
Will evaluate whether small towns receive their fair share of state resources and support local government grant capacity.

vt-aud-2026-kronick-ivar.name: Ivar Kronick
vt-aud-2026-kronick-ivar.bio: Former city councilor in Massachusetts and business owner; handles financial audits for an international manufacturing firm in Manchester.

positions.stance: Will publish a list of all entities the office audits, with audit dates and status of report recommendations.
Will refer appropriate investigations to the Attorney General's office and post all referrals on the Auditor's website.
Commits to keep the office "nonpartisan and objective at all times."
Will oversee regular, independent audits of state agencies and publish easy-to-understand reports for the public.

vt-ag-2026-clark-charity.name: Charity R. Clark
vt-ag-2026-clark-charity.bio: Attorney General of Vermont since 2023; former Chief of Staff and Assistant Attorney General in the Vermont Attorney General's Office.

positions.stance: Running to continue "protecting Vermont and Vermonters from federal overreach by the Trump Administration," including lawsuits against the administration.
Sued Meta and TikTok over harm to children and champions a data privacy bill.
Supports "our right to abortion," including suing the FDA to make medication abortion more accessible.
Sued pharmaceutical benefit managers over their role in inflated prescription drug costs.
"Charity prioritizes public safety, prosecuting violent crimes and sexual crimes against children."

wy-sos-2026-short-robert.name: Robert Short
wy-sos-2026-short-robert.bio: Three-term Converse County Commissioner and business owner in energy, agriculture, retail, and tourism.

positions.stance: Dedicated to upholding the "full range of Constitutional and statutory responsibilities" of the office, including careful stewardship of state lands.
Will work to stop those who use Wyoming's privacy laws to create sham corporations and unfairly compete.
Commits to ensuring Wyoming's elections "are conducted in a fair, honest, and accurate manner."
Will protect citizens from fraudulent investment schemes like cryptocurrency scams and ensure firms comply with state rules.

wy-aud-2026-racines-kristi.name: Kristi Racines
wy-aud-2026-racines-kristi.bio: Wyoming State Auditor; Certified Public Accountant and former Chief Fiscal Officer of Wyoming's judiciary.

positions.stance: Put Wyoming's checkbook online at WyOpen.gov and worked to pass a law preserving it.
"I believe in a right-sized, bite-sized government," citing reduced budget requests for the Auditor's office.
Has voted on the State Loan and Investment Board to invest in small communities, particularly infrastructure.
Brings "a balanced approach to the management of state lands, optimizing multiple uses with a respect for our traditional industries."

wy-treas-2026-meier-curt.name: Curt Meier
wy-treas-2026-meier-curt.bio: Wyoming State Treasurer, businessman, and former state legislator of nearly 25 years.

positions.stance: Will continue managing Wyoming's investments "with discipline and care" to achieve strong returns while protecting long-term stability.
Believes government "should live within its means," with careful budgeting and responsible spending.
Committed to upholding the U.S. and Wyoming Constitutions, with decisions guided by law rather than political pressure.
Says strong financial management helps Wyoming remain independent from federal mandates and reduce reliance on volatile revenue.
Will continue working to return unclaimed property so citizens can reclaim what is rightfully theirs.
